statement: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-3}$ for $x\ne3$. Find $f^{-1}(x)$ and state its domain.
solution:
Set $y=\dfrac{2x+1}{x-3}$ and solve for $x$:
$$y(x-3)=2x+1\quad\Rightarrow\quad yx-3y=2x+1\quad\Rightarrow\quad x(y-2)=3y+1,$$
so $x=\dfrac{3y+1}{y-2}$. Therefore
$$f^{-1}(x)=\frac{3x+1}{x-2},$$
with domain $x\ne2$ (the range of $f$).
hints: Write $y=f(x)$ and rearrange to make $x$ the subject.
Collect the $x$ terms on one side.
Swap $x$ and $y$ at the end and note excluded values.
